Forget AT&T and Verizon: Crown Castle Has More to Lose From Starlink's 40x Upgrade ©@Seasonal via Canva, @Oleksii Mach via Canva
Key Takeaways

Elon Musk said SpaceX's next direct-to-cell satellites will have 40x the bandwidth of today's, and that AT&T and Verizon may lose some revenue.

Crown Castle has more at stake than either carrier, since AT&T and Verizon pay 51% of its tower rent.

AT&T leases carrying $643 million of Crown's annualized cash rent come up for renewal in 2028, while American Tower relies far less on the two carriers.

Crown carries the risk until SpaceX signs a lease, and its 2027 outlook in early February is the next test.

Elon Musk thinks AT&T (T:NYSE) and Verizon (VZ:NYSE) will be fine. Their landlord, Crown Castle (CCI:NYSE), is in a tougher spot.

At the New York Times DealBook Summit on Nov. 18, Musk said SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) starts launching a direct-to-cell constellation next year that will "have 40 times the bandwidth of the current direct-to-cell version one." He doesn't expect the carriers to "go out of business or anything," but he added: "maybe they'll lose some revenue here."

That's a much bigger deal for Crown, which collects half its tower rent from those two and, unlike American Tower (AMT:NYSE), has nothing else to lean on.

Half the rent comes from two tenants

Since selling its fiber and small cell businesses on May 1, Crown owns only towers. AT&T paid 28% of its third-quarter annualized site rental revenue, Verizon 23%, and T-Mobile, whose T-Satellite service already runs on Starlink, 42%.

American Tower rents to the same carriers, but AT&T and Verizon made up just 31% of its 2025 revenue, according to its annual report, against 49% of Crown's. And cash revenue from its data centers grew 16.3% in the third quarter.

Crown has no such cushion. Beyond its lease escalators, its growth comes from carriers adding equipment to its towers, which a carrier losing revenue to a satellite rival has less reason to do. Analysts already expect very little growth:

Crown Castle (CCI): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

Analysts see $4.19 billion of revenue in 2028, still below the $4.26 billion Crown booked in 2025, before DISH's rent disappeared. Those estimates predate Musk's comments, and with the new satellites not launching until next year, there's little reason for them to move yet.

title: AST SpaceMobile Stock Gets FCC Approval for Direct to Device Service

AST SpaceMobile secured FCC approval for direct-to-device satellite service and outlined plans for intermittent nationwide coverage by late 2026 across key markets including the US, Canada, Japan, Saudi Arabia and the UK.

The combination of regulatory clearance and rollout plans, backed by partnerships with AT&T and Verizon, puts greater attention on AST SpaceMobile's execution, capital use and timeline risk in building a usable space-based cellular network.

We will now see how AST SpaceMobile's high-risk rollout story is affected by this new FCC approval for direct-to-device service.

Spot similar high-risk satellite and space infrastructure rollouts by scanning the hand-picked 52 AI infrastructure stocks that could sit alongside AST SpaceMobile in a telecom-meets-orbit portfolio.

AST SpaceMobile Investment Narrative Recap

To own AST SpaceMobile, you need to believe a global direct to phone satellite network can move from concept to a functioning commercial platform. According to HedgeY, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the real swing factor is execution across manufacturing, launches, regulation and carrier integration all working in sync. The fresh FCC approval tightens focus on whether intermittent coverage by 2026 and continuous service by 2027 remain realistic milestones.

The biggest short term catalyst is still getting enough BlueBird satellites into orbit and stitched into live service with AT&T, Verizon and other partners. Timeline slippage into mid 2027 and reliance on third party rockets keep launch bottlenecks front and center. Competition from SpaceX's direct to cell push compresses AST SpaceMobile's performance edge, so any extra delay in deployment now bites harder.

The most relevant recent development around this news is Elon Musk flagging next generation SpaceX direct to cell satellites with much higher target bandwidth. That move narrows AST SpaceMobile's technical lead and pushes investors to pay more attention to coverage density, reliability and integration with terrestrial networks rather than headline peak speeds.

Against that backdrop, the Deutsche Bank Global Space and Defense Tech Summit on 17 November 2026 becomes more than a marketing stop. It is an opportunity for AST SpaceMobile to update how it will manage launch access, capital use and competitive positioning after the FCC approval. The clearer management can be on execution milestones and risk controls, the more useful the event could be for anyone tracking near term catalysts.

BARTLETT, Tenn., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SurgePays, Inc. (NASDAQ: SURG) ("SurgePays" or the "Company"), a fintech company that launches and runs wireless brands, today announced its financial results for the third quarter and first nine-month period ended September 30, 2026.

"During the third quarter we strategically focused SurgePays' business model on our core prepaid wireless and fintech businesses, completing the sale of ClearLine and reporting our first full quarter under the amended AT&T agreement. Third quarter revenue totaled $17.3 million,(1) an increase of 6.5% sequentially, and nine-month revenue totaled $49.5 million, up 21.3% over the same period last year. Our point of sale and prepaid services business grew 15.1% year-over-year, while general and administrative expenses declined 15.4%. With this focus and a stronger balance sheet, we are positioned to grow on infrastructure we have already built. That is how we intend to build value for the Company," said Brian Cox, Chief Executive Officer of SurgePays.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

Revenue of $17.27 million, up 6.5% from $16.20 million in the second quarter of 2026 and down 7.6% from $18.68 million in the third quarter of 2025. Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $49.45 million, up 21.3% from $40.78 million in the prior year period.

Point-of-Sale and Prepaid Services segment revenue of $15.10 million, up 15.1% from $13.12 million in the prior year quarter. Nine-month segment revenue of $43.90 million was up 43.2%.

Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) segment revenue of $2.08 million, compared with $5.56 million in the prior year quarter. The decrease reflects the pause in new user intake by the Company's Eligible Telecommunications Carrier following an audit delay in the fourth quarter of 2025, as described in the Company's Form 10-Q.

MVNO segment gross margin improved to (23.1)% from (47.2)%, and the MVNO gross loss narrowed to $0.48 million from $2.63 million. The quarter was the first full quarter under the amended AT&T agreement.

Total gross loss of $2.84 million, compared with $2.60 million in the prior year quarter. Point-of-Sale and Prepaid Services gross margin was (16.4)% compared with 0.2%, and the Company expects to focus on improving gross margin in that segment during the remainder of 2026.

General and administrative expenses of $3.68 million, down 15.4% from $4.35 million. Nine-month general and administrative expenses of $11.82 million were down 10.1%.

Income from operations of $20.65 million, compared with a loss from operations of $6.95 million in the prior year quarter, including the $27.17 million non-cash gain on the sale of the ClearLine platform assets.

Net income available to common stockholders of $18.11 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, or $0.41 per basic share and $0.34 per diluted share, which includes a non-cash gain of $27.17 million on the sale of the ClearLine platform assets, compared with a net loss of $7.49 million, or $(0.38) per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Nine-month net income was $7.35 million compared with a net loss of $22.21 million.

Net cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 improved to $12.49 million from $17.73 million.

Cash and cash equivalents of $4.68 million at September 30, 2026, compared with $1.73 million at December 31, 2025.

Total stockholders' equity was $7.85 million, compared with a stockholders' deficit of $15.40 million at December 31, 2025.

title: Verizon CEO Pushes Back: “No Secret Sauce” in Musk’s Plan to Make SpaceX a US Carrier

Verizon CEO Pushes Back: "No Secret Sauce" in Musk's Plan to Make SpaceX a US Carrier ©U.S. Air Force photo and kb group via Canva
Key Takeaways

Verizon CEO Dan Schulman says SpaceX would need four to six years and about $300 billion to copy Verizon's network, with "no secret sauce" at the end of it.

SpaceX's plan to become a U.S. carrier knocked about $50 billion off the combined market value of Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile.

SpaceX is putting most of its capital into AI data centers and has pushed its next-generation phone service back to early 2028.

With T-Mobile reselling Starlink and Verizon and AT&T signed up with AST SpaceMobile, Schulman has the better of the argument for now.

Verizon (VZ:NYSE) CEO Dan Schulman has heard Elon Musk's plan to turn SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) into a major U.S. phone carrier, and he isn't panicking.

The plan, announced last month, knocked about $50 billion off the combined market value of Verizon, AT&T (T:NYSE) and T-Mobile (TMUS:NASDAQ). Verizon fell 9% that day, its worst day since 2002.

Schulman told Fortune on its Titans and Disruptors of Industry podcast that Musk would spend four to six years and about $300 billion building a copy of Verizon:

"At the end of the day, he might have a network that is pretty much exactly like our network today. There's no secret sauce, there's no magic wand, there's no structural cost advantage that will come out. He'll have a network, and in four years, five, six years, he'll be the sixth entrant into the market."

Musk sees something much bigger. He posted on X last week that "there will ultimately be over 100k SpaceX communications satellites, most of which will be V4 or V5. Good chance that this system carries about half of global traffic."

If he's right, that's a problem for every carrier, and for AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ), Verizon's and AT&T's satellite partner.

Schulman has reason to take SpaceX seriously. Verizon is defending a huge revenue base that barely grows. So any customers Starlink takes would come straight off the top line. Analysts expect its revenue to inch from $138 billion in 2025 to $144 billion in 2028, under 2% a year:

title: Implied Volatility Surging for Tutor Perini Stock Options

Trading disclosure

Investors in Tutor Perini Corporation TPC need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec. 18, 2026 $45.00 Put had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Tutor Perini shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Tutor Perini is a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) in the Building Products - Heavy Construction industry that ranks in the Top 18% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimate for the current quarter, while none have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from $1.29 per share to $1.33 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Tutor Perini right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

EchoStar Is the Real Winner of Starlink's 40x Phone Upgrade: About 262 Million SpaceX Shares ©NASA/Kim Shiflett and SUMALI IBNU CHAMID from Alemedia.id via Canva
Key Takeaways

Elon Musk said on Nov. 18 that SpaceX's next direct-to-cell satellites, launching in 2027, will have 40x today's bandwidth, and that AT&T and Verizon may lose some revenue.

That upgrade runs on spectrum EchoStar sold to SpaceX for about $19.6 billion, a price that includes roughly 262 million SpaceX shares.

Morgan Stanley says those shares could eventually be worth almost $40 billion, more than EchoStar's whole market value when the firm initiated coverage in September.

AT&T, Verizon and AST SpaceMobile have businesses to defend or prove, while EchoStar's risk is that its stake tracks all of SpaceX, where AI compute is now over half of revenue.

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) wants to sell phone service, and Elon Musk just told AT&T (T:NYSE) and Verizon (VZ:NYSE) what that could cost them: "maybe they'll lose some revenue here."

But the listed company with the most riding on Starlink's phone upgrade is EchoStar (ECHO:NASDAQ). It sold SpaceX the spectrum the upgrade runs on, and it's due about 262 million SpaceX shares as part of the price.

That puts EchoStar in a far better spot than AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ), the carriers' satellite partner.

40x, down from "more than 100"

At the New York Times DealBook Summit on Nov. 18, Andrew Ross Sorkin asked Musk whether SpaceX would buy an American telecom company. Musk laid out his plan instead: SpaceX starts launching its version 2 constellation next year, which will "have 40 times the bandwidth of the current direct-to-cell version one." He had claimed "more than 100 times" on X in October.

Today's service covers texting and a short list of apps where there's no cell signal. And while Musk doesn't expect the carriers to "go out of business or anything," the revenue they could lose comes from their most profitable business.

TIKR tracks 9 analysts on EchoStar. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on EchoStar, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See EchoStar's Analyst Ratings

EchoStar already got paid

EchoStar agreed to the sales in 2025, and SpaceX's S-1 puts the total at about $19.6 billion, with roughly $11.1 billion of it paid in about 261.8 million SpaceX shares at a fixed $42.40 each. SpaceX went public in June at $135 a share, so at the IPO price alone those shares were worth about $35 billion.

Not a bad trade.

Morgan Stanley analyst Sean Diffley initiated coverage of EchoStar at Buy with a $134 price target in September. He expects EchoStar to get the shares when the deal closes in November 2027 and says they could eventually be worth almost $40 billion, against EchoStar's market value then of roughly $27 billion. He called the gap "too wide to ignore."

title: Nokia vs. AT&T: Which Telecom Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Nokia vs. AT&T: Which Telecom Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool
Sun, November 22, 2026 at 6:23 PM MST 5 min read
NOK
T
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Connectivity serves as the backbone of the modern economy, but choosing between infrastructure and services requires careful analysis. Investing in Nokia Oyj (NYSE:NOK) or AT&T (NYSE:T) involves balancing network equipment growth against steady subscription revenue.

Nokia focuses on the hardware and software that make networks run, while AT&T is a retail giant providing wireless and fiber service to millions. This comparison examines their business models, balance sheets, and valuations to determine which stock is better for your portfolio.

The case for Nokia Oyj

Nokia is a global connectivity infrastructure company that builds networks across fixed, mobile, IP, optical, and data center systems. The company serves communications service providers, governments, and large enterprises while operating in approximately 130 countries with roughly 78,000 employees. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue, which helps diversify its revenue streams across various regions and sectors.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $22.6 billion, representing revenue growth of 4.1%. The company reported net income of $858.1 million during this period. This growth reflects ongoing investments in network technology as service providers around the world continue to upgrade their existing infrastructure.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.2x, indicating a low level of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio of 1.6x shows the company has more than enough assets to cover its short-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was $1.6 billion, which is the cash remaining after operating costs and equipment spending.

The case for AT&T

As one of the largest players among communication stocks, AT&T provides essential wireless and broadband services. The company serves approximately 145 million wireless subscribers in North America and maintains a long-term partnership with organizations such as the U.S. soccer league. Its customer segments range from individual consumers to large multinational corporations and government bodies through its FirstNet service, a dedicated network for first responders.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached $128.9 billion, supported by revenue growth of 3.5%. The company generated net income of $13.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of 10.2%. This net margin represents the percentage of revenue that remains as profit after all expenses are paid.
